policies.title: Data Center Investment Tax Exemption Program (20 ILCS 605/605-1025)
key_terms: Requires at least $250 million in capital investment over a 60-month period
Requires at least 20 new full-time-equivalent jobs tied to data center operations or maintenance
New jobs' total compensation must equal or exceed 120% of the county's median full-time wage
Data center must achieve carbon neutrality or a green-building certification
20% tax credit on construction wages, but only in designated underserved areas
Exemption runs up to 20 years as renewable 5-year certificates contingent on continued compliance
policies.summary: Illinois's data center sales-tax exemption program conditions eligibility on a $250M+ investment, at least 20 jobs paid above 120% of county median wage, and a carbon-neutrality or green-building certification, administered via a certification/MOU process with DCEO. As of July 1, 2026 the department stopped accepting new applications under a governor's directive issued June 5, 2026.
policies.source_title: Illinois DCEO — Data Center Investment Tax Exemptions and Credits

policies.title: Governor Pritzker directive pausing new Data Center Investment Program agreements
key_terms: Directs DCEO to pause processing new Data Center Investment Program agreements starting July 1, 2026
Issued after the General Assembly failed to pass the POWER Act (HB 5513) reforms by the May 31, 2026 spring-session deadline
Agreements entered into before July 1, 2026 remain honored and unaffected
Governor cited energy affordability, grid reliability, water depletion and community impacts as the reasons a long-term framework is needed
policies.summary: Gov. JB Pritzker directed DCEO to stop processing new Data Center Investment Program tax-exemption agreements as of July 1, 2026, after the legislature failed to pass his requested data center reform package (the POWER Act) by the spring 2026 deadline. Existing agreements are unaffected; Pritzker said he would push the issue again in the November veto session.
policies.source_title: Office of Gov. JB Pritzker — Gov. Pritzker Pauses New Data Center Tax Incentives

policies.title: House Enrolled Act 1210 — data center local sales/use tax revenue sharing
key_terms: Authorizes a host county or municipality to require a quarterly payment of up to 1% of the state sales/use tax that would otherwise be exempted on a qualified data center's electricity purchases
Applies to data centers whose permits/certificates are issued after June 30, 2026
Locality controls how the collected funds are used
Indiana Department of Revenue must report payment amounts to requesting jurisdictions
Left the underlying state sales/use tax exemption for data centers intact; no statewide moratorium and no equipment-purchase PILOT provision
policies.summary: Indiana's HEA 1210, signed March 12, 2026 and effective July 1, 2026, lets host counties and cities collect up to 1% of the sales/use tax data centers would otherwise not pay on their electricity bills, directed back to the local government. A broader companion bill (HB 1333) that would have added an equipment PILOT and eased farmland siting stalled in the Senate; only the narrower electricity revenue-share provision became law.
policies.source_title: Server Country — Indiana Data Center Policy (HEA 1210 summary)

policies.title: Executive Order 658 — data center development framework
key_terms: Applies to data centers with peak electricity demand over 25 MW
Developers must submit a community benefits agreement reviewed by the Office of Environmental Justice and Equity before permits issue
Bans permitting agencies from using non-disclosure agreements with data center projects
Requires local approval before state permitting proceeds
Requires procurement of incremental clean electricity to match the facility's annual consumption, with an alternative compliance payment option by Dec 31 2026
policies.summary: Gov. Maura Healey's Sept. 8, 2026 executive order conditions state permits for data centers over 25 MW on a community benefits agreement vetted by the state's environmental justice office, a ban on NDAs between agencies and developers, prior local approval, and a clean-energy matching requirement. It is a conditions-based framework, not a pause on permitting.
policies.source_title: National Law Review — Massachusetts Conditions Large Data Center Permits on Community Agreements

resources.title: WBUR — Proposed data centers subjected to local approvals under Gov. Healey's order

policies.title: Aspire Program — community benefits agreement condition
key_terms: A developer seeking Aspire tax-credit support must obtain a letter of support from the chief executive of the host municipality
Must enter into both a Community Benefits Agreement and a separate Redevelopment Agreement with the project's municipal governing body
NJEDA operates a Data Center Municipal Resource Hub to help host municipalities evaluate and negotiate these agreements
Aspire Program paused new applications effective 5:00pm EDT July 23, 2026 because demand exceeded available resources; applications expected to reopen fall 2026 with revised criteria
policies.summary: New Jersey's Aspire redevelopment tax-credit program, available to data center and other large projects, conditions state support on the developer signing a Community Benefits Agreement plus a Redevelopment Agreement with the host municipality, and securing the municipality's letter of support. NJEDA has paused new Aspire applications since July 2026 pending a program review.

resources.title: NJEDA — Data Center Municipal Resource Hub

policies.title: Executive Order 2026-005 — Nevada Standard for Responsible Data Center Development
key_terms: Developers seeking a partial tax abatement must pay the Local School Support Tax in full (no abatement on it)
Must maintain a combined sales and use tax rate of at least 4.6%

Must execute a binding 'Nevada Community Support Commitment' before Board review, covering water standards, infrastructure cost responsibility, grid-reliability/emergency curtailment obligations, siting, workforce development and community benefits
Governor's Office of Economic Development must publish standard commitment terms by Nov. 6, 2026
Material violations can suspend the abatement and trigger recapture; grid-reliability breaches during emergencies are default with no cure period
policies.summary: Gov. Joe Lombardo's executive order conditions Nevada's partial data-center tax abatements on a binding 'Nevada Community Support Commitment' covering water, grid-cost responsibility, emergency curtailment, workforce and community benefits, plus full payment of the Local School Support Tax. It applies only to pending abatement applications, not retroactively.
policies.source_title: News 3 Las Vegas — Nevada Governor signs executive order setting new rules for state data center development

policies.title: Governor DeWine directive pausing new data center tax exemption requests
key_terms: Directs the chair of the Ohio Tax Credit Authority to pause consideration of new data center sales/use tax exemption requests
Pause runs while the Ohio General Assembly's Joint Data Center Committee studies data center growth and local benefits of the exemptions
Existing/previously granted exemptions are unaffected; one already-pending request was still considered at the next scheduled meeting
Explicitly described by the Governor's office as not a data center ban
policies.summary: Gov. Mike DeWine directed Ohio's Tax Credit Authority to stop accepting new data-center sales/use tax exemption requests starting May 27, 2026, pending a legislative study by the Joint Data Center Committee of the exemptions' costs and local benefits. Existing exemptions, representing $27.2B in prior investment, are untouched.
policies.source_title: The Clermont Sun — Governor DeWine Announces Pause of Data Center Tax Exemption
